note: Guilds and Orders (the nine workshops, their policies and AI weights) and Spells (special projects, scholars, rewards and scars). Equipment names are the archetypes of the warfare spec section 3; technology names are those of the technology specs; categories are the zin_cat_* of 07_industry_and_electronics_techs section 2.2. Pictures are keys of the icon catalog.

methods.name: Fair Dealing
methods.desc: Honest weights and a plain ledger mean fewer disputes and cheaper work.

methods.name: Guild Habits
methods.desc: Journeymen pass on their tricks, and the work gets faster each season.

methods.name: The Master's Pace
methods.desc: A master's hand sets the pace, and the line settles into a steady rhythm.

standing.name: Patrons
standing.desc: Lords and merchants give the guild their custom, and fund its study.

standing.name: The Journeymen's Hall
standing.desc: A hall where the guild keeps its books and trains its young. More work can be taken at once.

standing.name: The Counting-House
standing.desc: The guild's coin is counted, lent and returned with interest.

workshops.name: The Smiths' Guild
workshops.desc: Smiths of every town who answer to one guild and one hall. They shape arms for all comers.

p.name: Hardened Edges
p.desc: Edges are quenched twice and last a campaign.

p.name: Cleaving Blades
p.desc: Blades are weighted for the downward stroke.

p.name: Piercing Points
p.desc: Spearheads are forged to find the seam in the plate.

cap.name: The Master's Mark
cap.desc: A guild mark that every buyer trusts, and every thief copies.

workshops.name: The Bowyers' Hall
workshops.desc: Yew, horn and sinew. The Hall fixes the length of every bow and the price of every string.

p.name: Longer Draw
p.desc: Bows are cut a hand longer and shoot a pace further.

p.name: Waxed Strings
p.desc: Strings keep their strength through rain and frost.

p.name: Bodkin Heads
p.desc: Narrow points that find the gap in mail.

cap.name: The Composite Secret
cap.desc: Horn, wood and sinew glued in layers by a method the Hall will never write down.

workshops.name: The Armourers' Hall
workshops.desc: Mail-makers and plate-smiths under one roof. A knight is only as safe as the Hall's last proof.

p.name: Riveted Mail
p.desc: Each ring is riveted shut, and the mail turns a blade.

p.name: Padded Under-Coats
p.desc: A quilted coat beneath the mail spreads each blow.

p.name: Plate Harness
p.desc: Shaped plates over the chest and thigh, proof against a bodkin.

cap.name: The Tempered Plate
cap.desc: Plate hardened in three oils and proved with a crossbow before it leaves the Hall.

workshops.name: The Shipwrights' Guild
workshops.desc: Keel-layers, caulkers and rope-makers. Its slips stand by every harbour worth the name.

p.name: Cleaner Lines
p.desc: Hulls are shaped long and low and slip through the water.

p.name: Doubled Timbers
p.desc: Ribs set closer and planking doubled at the waterline.

p.name: Long Water-Casks
p.desc: Holds are fitted for longer voyages between harbours.

cap.name: The Master Shipwrights
cap.desc: Hulls signed by the masters of the Guild, who stake their name on every keel.

workshops.name: The Engineers' Lodge
workshops.desc: A lodge of masons and carpenters sworn to share what they learn of siege-engines and walls.

p.name: Heavier Arms
p.desc: Throwing-arms are cut longer and counterweighted.

p.name: Better Windlasses
p.desc: Windlasses with extra pawls, so cords seldom snap.

p.name: Iron-Shod Bolts
p.desc: Bolts shod in iron, aimed to pierce a great hide.

cap.name: The Great Engines
cap.desc: The Lodge's finest, raised once in a generation and spoken of for a hundred years.

workshops.name: The Royal Stud
workshops.desc: Mares, stallions and the grooms who know every bloodline. The Stud answers to the crown.

p.name: Hardy Stock
p.desc: Mares crossed for stamina; mounts keep the road longer.

p.name: Charger Lines
p.desc: Heavier stock bred for the first shock.

p.name: Steady Nerves
p.desc: Colts are raised among drums and banners and do not shy.

cap.name: The Great Studs
cap.desc: The Stud's best bloodlines, entered in a book kept under lock.

workshops.name: The Wardsmiths
workshops.desc: An order sworn to lanterns, glass and the old songs. They carry their craft from house to house and keep its secret.

p.name: Hallowed Wicks
p.desc: The wicks are blessed at the turn of every season.

p.name: Close-Set Wards
p.desc: Wards are set so close that a gap cannot open between them.

p.name: Piercing Light
p.desc: A warded lantern turned to a narrow beam, which no ordinary armour turns.

cap.name: The Warded Cloth
cap.desc: Cloth woven with wards, lit by an oath, and carried by those who keep it.

workshops.name: The Leaf-Forges
workshops.desc: Elven smiths who forge in the open under the trees and sing the metal into shape.

p.name: Silver-Leaf Edges
p.desc: Blades are drawn thin and bright, and take any edge.

p.name: Long Songs
p.desc: Songs that last a whole night set the temper deep.

p.name: Starlit Points
p.desc: Points ground by moonlight, which pierce what others turn.

cap.name: The Song-Forged
cap.desc: Blades that were sung, not hammered, and which hold their edge for ages.

workshops.name: The Grave-Forges
workshops.desc: Smiths bound by oath to their dark lord, who forge in deep halls where the flame burns cold.

p.name: Rimed Blades
p.desc: Blades quenched in grave-frost and edged with bone.

p.name: Bound Metal
p.desc: Metal bound to hold its edge by oath rather than by craft.

p.name: Deep Plate
p.desc: Plates beaten in the deep halls, heavy and nearly proof against spears.

cap.name: The Deep Forging
cap.desc: The Forges' mastery of metal that was never meant to be worked by living hands.

policies.name: Guild Charters
policies.desc: A royal charter fixes the guild's prices and its privileges. Work is cheaper to commission.

policies.name: Master's Marks
policies.desc: Every piece leaves the hall under a master's mark and he answers for its fall.

policies.name: Royal Warrants
policies.desc: The crown buys the guild's whole output at a fixed price. The line runs full.

scholarTraits.name: Gifted
scholarTraits.desc: A mind that seems to see the whole working at once.

scholarTraits.name: Loremaster
scholarTraits.desc: Knows the old books better than the librarians who keep them.

scholarTraits.name: Artificer
scholarTraits.desc: Happier at the bench than at the lectern.

scholarTraits.name: Quick Student
scholarTraits.desc: Learns a rite on the first telling.

scholarTraits.name: Steady Hand
scholarTraits.desc: Never hurries a circle, and a working under his hand seldom goes wrong.

scholarTraits.name: Restless
scholarTraits.desc: Cannot leave a working alone. Quick, and quick to err.

scholarTraits.name: Cautious
scholarTraits.desc: Checks the circle thrice before lighting it.

scholarTraits.name: Elder Memory
scholarTraits.desc: Remembers the rites as they were first taught, long before the Fourth Age.

scholarTraits.name: Keeper of Old Lore
scholarTraits.desc: Holds a few leaves of lore that no one else has seen.

marked.name: Marked
marked.desc: A working went wrong and left a mark on the scholar. Until it is lifted, he works slower and sees less.

scars.name: Hollow Ground
scars.desc: The working went wrong. The ground here is dull and sour, and the wagon-roads sink.

scars.name: Wrecked Moorings
scars.desc: The working went wrong. The quay-stones are cracked and the water here is sour.

scars.name: Scorched Roost
scars.desc: The working went wrong. The perches are charred and the beasts will not settle.

scars.name: Blighted Wellspring
scars.desc: The working went wrong. What came up from the deep stones has soured the whole country.

hallowed.name: Hallowed Ground
hallowed.desc: A circle of wards keeps this land. Foes tire here, and friends are fed.

wildSurge.name: Wild Surge
wildSurge.desc: A working slipped its leash for a night. The land is unsettled, and the hosts uneasy.

spells.name: The Lantern Ward
spells.desc: A chain of wards, lit in a certain order, so that any host sheltering behind it cannot be surprised. The lanterns burn with no flame at all.

spells.name: Hallowed Ground
spells.desc: A ring of stones set in the field, sung over by the wardens. No foe lingers here, and friends find the supply wagons already there.

spells.name: Calm Waters
spells.desc: A rite sung over the harbour on the first tide of spring, to ease the storms for a season and the fleets that sail through them.

spells.name: Sea-Sight
spells.desc: A glass ground under the rite, so that a lookout sees farther over the water than his eyes alone can.

spells.name: Dragon-Speech
spells.desc: Old words that quiet a great beast's temper. A rider who knows them is less often thrown, and his mount flies a little further.

spells.name: Wind-Reading
spells.desc: Flags, feathers and a wise old keeper, taught to read the sky for a day ahead.

spells.name: The Wellspring Rite
spells.desc: A rite worked at a deep spring, where the stone is slow to give. When it holds, essence flows from the earth for the whole realm.

spells.name: Lifting the Curse
spells.desc: A rite of unbinding, sung over a ruined place by the best scholars of the realm. A scar of earlier workings fades, and the marked among the scholars are made whole.

spells.name: The Grave-Binding Rite
spells.desc: A rite worked in the deep halls to bind the grave hosts more tightly to their lord's will, so that they hold together under heavier blows.

rewards.name: Steady Work
rewards.desc: A quiet season. The scholar learns a little and loses nothing.

rewards.name: Steady Work
rewards.desc: A fruitful season. The scholar learns a good deal from the working.

rewards.name: Steady Work
rewards.desc: A season of insight. The scholar learns more than a decade of study could give.

rewards.name: Insight
rewards.desc: The working gave a clear sight of a nearby craft. The realm's craftsmen will learn it faster.

rewards.name: A Clear Morning
rewards.desc: The working went more easily than anyone expected.

rewards.name: A Wasted Night
rewards.desc: The circle was lit and the words sung, but nothing came of it.

rewards.name: Burned Hands
rewards.desc: A flare of sparks from the stones. The scholar is hurt and the work set back.

rewards.name: Scarred Ground
rewards.desc: Something went wrong in the working, and the place where it was worked will not forget it.

rewards.name: Marked
rewards.desc: A mark is left on the scholar, who does not know yet how to be rid of it.

rewards.name: Wild Surge
rewards.desc: The working slipped its leash for a night. The land is unsettled, and the hosts uneasy.

rewards.name: Lost Notes
rewards.desc: Leaves from the scholar's notebook were lost in the night, and a month of work with them.
